title: How to brush a child's teeth
what: A child's teeth need brushing from the very first tooth. Here is how to do it at home simply and calmly.
why: For all parents, from the first tooth until the child can brush alone.
duration: usually 2 minutes in the morning and evening
tell_doctor: If the gums bleed or are red
If there are dark or white spots on the teeth
If your child falls asleep with a bottle

prepare.title: Toothbrush
prepare.text: A soft children's toothbrush for their age. Replace it about every 3 months.

prepare.title: Toothpaste
prepare.text: Children's fluoride toothpaste. The amount depends on age, from a smear to a pea size, so check with your dentist.

prepare.title: Position
prepare.text: It is easy to stand behind your child, or lay them with their head on your lap.

bring: A mirror so your child can see
steps: Put a small amount of toothpaste on the brush
Hold your child so you can see their teeth
Brush each tooth with gentle circles
Let your child spit out the toothpaste, if they can
feel: Small children often resist, which is normal
A game, a song, or taking turns, "first me, then you," helps
after: Help brush until about school age
After the evening brushing, only water
Give sweets with meals, not between meals

faq.q: Should my child rinse after brushing?
faq.a: Usually advised only to spit, not to rinse with lots of water. Check with your dentist.

faq.q: What if my child won't let me brush?
faq.a: Do not give up: brush briefly but every day, and turn it into a game.

reminders.text: Time to brush your child's teeth before bed. After brushing, only water.
